user.title: Connect to Comelit Intercom
user.description: Enter the IP address of your Comelit intercom. Just leave the rest as-is: Home Assistant will automatically create its own dedicated user on the device and activate it locally (no cloud, no app). This needs the device web password (the factory default is 'comelit'). Advanced options: point at a user you paired yourself via the Comelit app, or paste an existing token.

data_description.port: ICONA Bridge port (default 64100 - leave as-is unless you use port forwarding)
data_description.web_password: Password of the device web UI on port 8080 (factory default 'comelit')
data_description.dedicated_user: Advanced: name or email of a user you created and paired via the app; its token is read from a device backup instead of creating a new user
data_description.token: Advanced: use an existing user token directly

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate Comelit Intercom
reauth_confirm.description: The token for {host} is no longer valid. Leave the token blank to auto-provision a fresh dedicated user (needs the device web password), or paste a token. The current token is shown below so you can copy it.

data_description.web_password: Password of the device web UI on port 8080 (factory default 'comelit')
data_description.dedicated_user: Advanced: name or email of a user you paired via the app
data_description.token: Current token (edit to change, or blank to re-provision)

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Comelit Intercom
reconfigure.description: Change the IP address or authentication for {host} without removing the integration.

data_description.web_password: Password of the device web UI on port 8080 (factory default 'comelit')
data_description.dedicated_user: Advanced: name or email of a user you paired via the app

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the device

data.open_door_in_call: Open doors inside the ring's call

data_description.enable_notifications: Receive real-time ring events via Comelit's cloud (FCM). Requires the device to have internet access.
data_description.push_token: Advanced: enroll push under a different ICONA token so a paired phone keeps its own notifications. Leave empty to use the main token.
data_description.enable_audio: Carry the entrance's G.711 audio in the camera stream (audible via the unmute control in the WebRTC view). Turn off if the audio track disturbs the HLS/video playback. Takes effect on the next stream reconnect.
data_description.auto_answer: Experimental: when the doorbell rings, automatically answer the incoming call (inbound two-way audio). May be unstable and, on shared/multi-unit entries, can affect other units. Leave off unless testing. Takes effect on reload.
data_description.face_recognition: Relay the monitor's own face-recognition results (models that advertise it, e.g. 6741W) as comelit_intercom_face events. The match is made by the monitor with Comelit's cloud. Takes effect on reload.
data_description.open_door_in_call: When Home Assistant holds a ring's call (the on-ring preview, or a call answered by speak or auto-answer), a door's open command is sent inside that call, as the app does, answering the preview first: the monitor then stops ringing. Needed on a 6741W, which ignores the usual open command while it rings. Off: the usual open command, as before.
data_description.verbose_logging: Log detailed protocol/video/audio internals (for bug reports). Also enable debug logging on the integration to capture everything.

speak.name: Speak at the entrance
speak.description: Say a message (text-to-speech) or play an audio file on the entrance panel's speaker. Mode "call" opens a short call to the panel, plays the audio and hangs up; it never interrupts a ring, a call or a live view: it waits up to "Max wait" for the panel to be free, otherwise it gives up and logs why. Mode "answer" answers the incoming call Home Assistant holds after a ring at once and speaks on it as soon as the audio is ready (the monitor may then lose that call). With "Open the door" it opens the door afterwards: inside the answered ring's call in mode "answer", with the usual open command in mode "call"; it never opens otherwise. "Prepare only" builds and caches the audio without any call. Experimental. Returns the outcome (spoken, door, reason, timings).

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: "call": open a new call once the panel is free. "answer": answer the incoming call of the current ring and speak on it (test it first: the monitor may lose the call, e.g. not open the gate).

answer_fallback.name: Fall back to call
answer_fallback.description: With mode "answer" and no incoming call to answer: open a new call instead (on) or give up (off).

open_door.name: Open the door
open_door.description: After the message (or right after answering, with no message), open the door. Mode "answer": inside the answered call, waiting at most 2 s for the panel's ACK and call end, then hang up (a 6741W sends neither and opens anyway). Mode "call": the usual open command, as the lock does. Off by default: without it the door is never opened.

door.name: Door
door.description: Name of the door to open (as in the device's opendoor address book). Default: the only door on this entrance.

prepare_only.name: Prepare only
prepare_only.description: Only build the audio and keep it in memory (no call), so a later speak with the same message starts at once. For warm-up automations.

message.name: Message
message.description: Text to say. Give this or a media content ID (or neither, with "Open the door").

media_content_id.name: Media content ID
media_content_id.description: Ready-made audio instead of a message: a media-source ID (local media or TTS), an absolute path in an allowed folder (allowlist_external_dirs) or an http(s) URL listed in allowlist_external_urls.

tts_entity.name: TTS engine
tts_entity.description: Text-to-speech entity (or legacy engine name). Default: Home Assistant's default engine.

language.name: Language
language.description: Language of the message. Default: Home Assistant's language. A short tag like "en" is matched to what the engine lists (e.g. "en-US").

voice.name: Voice
voice.description: Engine voice. Default: the engine's own. A clear, firm voice carries best through the panel's small speaker (e.g. "kore" on Google AI, "nova" on OpenAI).

options.name: TTS options
options.description: Extra options for the TTS engine.

cache.name: Cache
cache.description: Reuse Home Assistant's TTS cache and the audio kept in memory for repeated messages. Off: render the message again.

gain_db.name: Gain
gain_db.description: Extra gain in dB after normalising the audio to -1 dBFS (negative is quieter, positive may clip).

max_wait.name: Max wait
max_wait.description: How long to wait for the entrance to be free (ringing, in a call, live view) before giving up.

audio_wait.name: Audio wait
audio_wait.description: Advanced: after the call is answered, how long to wait for the panel's own audio (proof the audio path is open) before playing anyway.

lead_in.name: Lead-in
lead_in.description: Advanced: silence sent before the message starts.

transport.name: Transport
transport.description: Advanced: how to send the audio to the panel. "auto": the same transport as the call's video (TCP or UDP), in both modes. A 6741W plays the voice only over TCP (over UDP its speaker switches on but stays silent); its video arrives over TCP, so "auto" picks TCP.
